overview: Both shape which organisms show up and how — but selective media controls what grows, while differential media controls how growth looks.
genZNote: One's a bouncer, one's a stylist.

aspects.label: Purpose
aspects.valueA: Inhibits growth of unwanted organisms while allowing a target group to grow, isolating it from a mixed sample.
aspects.valueB: Allows multiple organism types to grow but produces visibly distinct colony appearances, distinguishing between them.

aspects.label: Composition
aspects.valueA: Contains inhibitory agents such as antibiotics, dyes, salts, or extreme pH that suppress non-target organisms.
aspects.valueB: Contains indicator substrates (e.g. specific sugars with a pH indicator, or a substrate cleaved differently by different organisms) that reveal metabolic differences visually.

aspects.label: Target Organisms
aspects.valueA: A specific group is favored (e.g. Gram-negative rods on a medium inhibiting Gram-positives).
aspects.valueB: No organism is excluded by the medium itself — differentiation happens after growth, based on appearance.

aspects.label: Expected Appearance
aspects.valueA: Only the target group (or a narrowed set) produces visible colonies; others are suppressed or absent.
aspects.valueB: Multiple organism types grow, but colonies differ in color, halo, or other visible traits based on their metabolic activity.

aspects.label: Limitations / Pitfalls
aspects.valueA: Some non-target organisms may still grow weakly ('breakthrough growth'), and some target organisms may be inhibited if sensitive to the selective agent.
aspects.valueB: Differentiation reflects a specific biochemical trait, not full identification — further testing is usually still needed.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Controls which organisms are able to grow at all.
aspects.valueB: Controls how different organisms appear once they've grown.

aspects.label: Primary Purpose / Indication
aspects.valueA: Isolating a target organism or group from a mixed/contaminated specimen.
aspects.valueB: Distinguishing between organisms that grow together, based on a visible metabolic trait.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Media formulated to inhibit unwanted organisms so a target group can be isolated.
aspects.valueB: Media formulated to reveal visible metabolic differences between organisms that are allowed to grow together.

aspects.label: Limitations
aspects.valueA: Selective pressure can occasionally suppress a slow-growing target along with the non-target flora.
aspects.valueB: A differential reaction on its own is rarely sufficient for a definitive identification.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: MacConkey agar is actually both — selective for Gram-negatives and differential for lactose fermentation. A great example to remember the distinction with.
overlay.memoryTrick: "Selective picks who's invited. Differential decides what they wear."
overlay.commonMisconception: Selective and differential are not mutually exclusive — many real media (e.g. MacConkey, EMB) do both jobs at once.
